headline: Floor 7 Resident Reports Reflection Showing 'Rooms That Don't Exist Behind Me'
subheadline: Latest Hartwell mirror anomaly includes detailed views of unfamiliar spaces; one resident claims to have seen 'a floor with no number'
summary: New reports from Hartwell Building's Floor 7 describe mirror reflections showing impossible architecture behind the viewer.
content:
The Hartwell Building's Floor 7 mirrors have exhibited strange behavior for decades. But the latest reports suggest the anomalies are evolving.

Three residents have independently reported that their reflections now show rooms behind them that do not correspond to actual Floor 7 hallways.

"I was checking my hair in the hallway mirror," said resident Patrick Liu, 34. "And behind my reflection, I could see... it wasn't the hallway. It was an office. Old-fashioned, with wooden desks and typewriters. There was a calendar on the wall. It said 1923."

Liu attempted to photograph the phenomenon, but his phone's camera showed only the normal hallway behind him.

Resident Amara Obi, 28, reported a different scene. "Behind my reflection was a room with no windows. Just filing cabinets, wall to wall. And there was someone in there, going through the files. They were wearing clothes from... I don't know, the 1950s? They didn't notice me. Or maybe they did and they just didn't look up."

The most disturbing account came from Margaret Holloway, 67, who previously reported her reflection blinking independently. Holloway claims she saw something even more unusual.

"The mirror showed a hallway behind me," Holloway said, "but the hallway had a floor indicator. Like in an elevator. And the number on the indicator was 13."

The Hartwell Building officially has no 13th floor. The elevator goes directly from 12 to 14. Building management has consistently denied the existence of any floor between them.

Omnicorp Holdings released a statement: "The mirrors on Floor 7 are standard mirrors, purchased from a standard mirror supplier, installed by standard contractors in 1987. They reflect what is in front of them. What residents choose to see in their reflections is a matter of personal perception."

When asked about the 1987 installation date, building historian Chen Wei (@HartwellSecrets) noted: "That's interesting, because the building permits show mirror installations on Floor 7 in 1987, 1991, 1995, 2002, 2008, 2014, and 2021. They keep replacing the mirrors. The reflections stay weird. It's almost like the mirrors aren't the problem."

Dr. Elena Martinez was contacted for comment on the physics of reflective anomalies. She responded via email: "I study quantum mechanics, not mirror ghosts. Please stop emailing me about the Hartwell Building. I don't know anything about it." The email was sent at 3:47 AM.

Residents have begun organizing a petition to have the Floor 7 mirrors removed entirely. Omnicorp Holdings has not responded to the petition, except to note that "mirror removal would constitute a lease violation."
author: Sandra Mitchell, Local News
